name: Wapu Auth – Social Login
author: victor88lm

sections.description:
Wapu Auth – Social Login provides seamless social authentication for your WordPress and WooCommerce store. Allow customers to register and log in with their Google accounts in just one click.

Key Features

  • One-Click Social Login – Customers can sign in with their Google account instantly
  • Customizable Button – Adjust colors, text, size, and style to match your theme
  • WooCommerce Integration – Automatically integrates with login, registration, and checkout forms
  • Analytics Dashboard – Track login statistics, user registrations, and activity
  • Domain Restrictions – Allow or block specific email domains
  • Sandbox Mode – Test with specific email addresses before going live
  • Activity Log – Monitor all login attempts and user actions
  • Popup Mode – Optional popup window for smoother login experience
  • Shortcode Support – Place the login button anywhere with [wapu_auth_button]
  • Custom Login/Register Forms – Three beautiful templates (Classic, Modern, Compact)

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.0 or higher
  • PHP 7.4 or higher
  • WooCommerce 7.0 or higher (optional but recommended)
  • SSL certificate (HTTPS)
  • Google Cloud Console account

Setup

  1. Create a project in Google Cloud Console
  2. Configure OAuth consent screen
  3. Create OAuth 2.0 credentials (Web application type)
  4. Add your redirect URI from the plugin settings
  5. Copy Client ID and Client Secret to the plugin

External Services

This plugin connects to external services only when specific features are used:

  1. Google OAuth / OpenID (required for Google login)

– Service endpoints:
– https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth
– https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token
– https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v2/userinfo
– https://accounts.google.com/.well-known/openid-configuration (connectivity checks)
– Data sent:
– During OAuth: client_id, redirect_uri, scope, state, authorization code.
– During user info fetch: OAuth access token in Authorization header.
– Data received:
– Google account ID, email, verified_email, name, avatar URL, locale.
– When sent:
– Only when a user clicks Google login or an admin runs connection diagnostics.
– Why:
– To authenticate users with Google and create/login WordPress accounts.
– Terms and privacy:
– https://policies.google.com/privacy
– https://policies.google.com/terms

  1. GeoIP providers (optional, disabled by default)

– Services:
– https://ipapi.co/
– https://ipwho.is/ (fallback)
– Data sent:
– Visitor IP address (for geolocation lookup).
– When sent:
– Only if GeoIP is enabled in plugin security settings.
– Why:
– To enrich activity logs with approximate country/city statistics.
– Terms and privacy:
– https://ipapi.co/privacy/
– https://ipwhois.io/privacy-policy/
– Compliance note:
– Site owners should enable this only with an appropriate legal basis and user consent where required.

  1. Google Analytics 4 event bridge (optional)

– Service:
– Uses the site’s existing gtag/GA4 setup if present.
– Data sent:
– Event names and labels related to login flow (login_start, success/error metadata).
– When sent:
– Only if analytics is enabled and a GA4 Measurement ID is configured in plugin settings.
– Why:
– To measure login funnel performance.
– Terms and privacy:
– https://policies.google.com/privacy
– https://policies.google.com/terms
– Compliance note:
– Site owners are responsible for obtaining any required user consent before enabling Analytics tracking.

  1. Google Fonts prefetch/caching hints (optional frontend optimization)

– Services:
– https://fonts.googleapis.com
– https://fonts.gstatic.com
– Data sent:
– Standard browser request metadata (IP, user-agent) to retrieve font CSS/assets.
– When sent:
– When frontend button assets are loaded and browser requests those resources.
– Why:
– To render button typography and improve UX consistency.
– Terms and privacy:
– https://policies.google.com/privacy
– https://policies.google.com/terms

External services compliance responsibility:
– This plugin provides technical integrations only.
– Site owners are responsible for privacy notices, consent banners, and legal configuration required in their jurisdiction before enabling GeoIP and/or Google Analytics features.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/wapu-auth-social-login/
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress
  3. Go to Wapu Auth in the admin menu to configure
  4. Follow the setup wizard to connect your Google API credentials
sections.faq:
Do I need a Google Cloud account?

Yes, you need to create a project in Google Cloud Console to get OAuth credentials.

Does this work without WooCommerce?

Yes! The plugin works on any WordPress site. WooCommerce integration is optional but adds automatic button placement on login/register/checkout forms.

Is HTTPS required?

Yes, Google OAuth requires HTTPS for production use.

Can I customize the button appearance?

Yes, the plugin includes a visual button editor with color pickers and live preview.

What social providers are supported?

Currently Google is supported. More providers may be added in future versions.
sections.changelog:
1.0.1

  • Fix: Admin notices now persist dismissal across page reloads.
  • Dev: PHPCS/WPCS coding standards improvements.

1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • Google OAuth login and registration
  • Customizable button with visual editor
  • Admin dashboard with analytics
  • Activity log with geo-location tracking
  • Domain restriction feature (whitelist/blacklist)
  • Sandbox mode for testing
  • Custom login/register form templates (Classic, Modern, Compact)
  • WooCommerce integration (optional)
  • Shortcode support: [wapu_auth_button], [wapu_auth_login_form], [wapu_auth_register_form]
  • Full i18n support (English + Spanish)
